title: Contractor Bill Verification Against BOQ
summary: Check every RA bill line against the work order BOQ, measurement records, previous bills and recovery rules, so billing engineers certify from a verified sheet instead of re-adding.

seo.title: RA Bill Verification Against BOQ with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that checks contractor RA bills against BOQ rates and quantities, measurement books, previous bills and recoveries, and flags exceptions for QS review.

problem.intro: Contractors raise running account bills every month with an abstract, measurement sheets and claims for extra items. Billing engineers check each line against the BOQ, the measurement book and the previous bill before the project manager signs off. With several contractors per tower, this check is where rate errors, quantity overruns and missed recoveries slip through.

pain_points.title: Cumulative quantities that drift
pain_points.detail: Up-to-date quantities claimed against an item can exceed the BOQ or the measured quantity, and the arithmetic of previous plus current is rarely redone in full.

pain_points.title: Rates and items outside the contract
pain_points.detail: Lines billed at a revised rate, or for items not in the BOQ, need an approved variation, but they look like any other line in a long abstract.

pain_points.title: Deductions and recoveries missed
pain_points.detail: Mobilisation advance recovery, retention, TDS, GST and labour cess each follow their own rule, and an error in one bill carries into the next.

pain_points.title: Free-issue material not reconciled
pain_points.detail: Cement and steel issued by the developer should reconcile with theoretical consumption, but the reconciliation is often skipped when payment is urgent.

solution.overview: We build a bill checking pipeline that reads the contractor's RA bill, abstract and measurement sheets, whether they arrive as Excel, PDF or scans, and matches each line to the work order BOQ. It recomputes cumulative quantities and amounts, compares rates with the contract, checks quantities against measurement book entries and BOQ limits, and applies your rules for advances, retention, material recovery, taxes and cess. Each line gets a status of matched, needs review or not in contract. The billing engineer works from this sheet, records decisions and certifies the bill in your usual system. The pipeline never certifies a bill or releases a payment.
capabilities: Extraction of RA bill abstracts and measurement sheets from Excel, PDF and scans
Line matching to BOQ items by code and description, including items the contractor has renamed
Recalculation of previous, current and up-to-date quantities and amounts
Rate check against the work order and approved variations, with non-BOQ items flagged
Rule-based deductions for mobilisation advance, retention, free-issue material, TDS, GST and labour cess
Theoretical versus issued consumption check for cement and steel

workflow.title: Receive the RA bill
workflow.detail: The contractor's bill, abstract and measurement sheets arrive by email or upload and are linked to the work order.

workflow.title: Extract bill lines
workflow.detail: Each line's item, description, unit, rate and previous, current and cumulative quantities are extracted.

workflow.title: Match to BOQ and measurements
workflow.detail: Lines are matched to BOQ items and compared with measurement book entries and approved variations.

workflow.title: Recalculate and apply rules
workflow.detail: Arithmetic, BOQ limits, rates and deductions are recomputed, and mismatches and non-BOQ items are flagged.

workflow.title: Billing engineer review
workflow.detail: The engineer reviews flagged lines with their source pages, accepts or corrects them and adds remarks.

workflow.title: Certify and record
workflow.detail: The verified sheet supports certification in your ERP, and decisions are kept for the next bill and for audit.

inputs: Contractor RA bill, abstract and measurement sheets
Work order with BOQ, rates and terms
Measurement book entries or site measurement records
Approved variation and extra item orders
Material issue register for free-issue cement and steel
outputs: Line-by-line verification sheet with matched, review and not-in-contract status
Recalculated bill abstract with proposed corrections
human_in_the_loop: The billing engineer or quantity surveyor reviews every flagged line and certifies the bill, and the project manager approves it under your delegation of authority. The pipeline proposes corrections but cannot change a certified amount or release a payment.
integrations: ERP or project accounting system such as SAP, Oracle or Farvision
Excel BOQ and bill formats used by your contractors
Email inbox used for bill submission
Document management system for work orders
Tally or your accounts system for payment processing
guardrails: No automatic certification or payment release
Every corrected figure shows the original value, the rule applied and the source
Rate and deduction rules versioned per work order
Non-BOQ items can only be accepted with a linked variation reference
QS team samples auto-matched lines every billing cycle
compliance_notes: Keeps an audit trail for contractor payments, including TDS and GST treatment as configured by your finance team.
Labour cess deductions follow the rules your finance team sets for each state and contract.

faqs.q: Our contractors all use different bill formats. Will it cope?
faqs.a: Yes. The extractor reads the bill's content rather than a fixed template and maps renamed or reworded items to BOQ codes. New formats are added to the test set during the pilot, and any line it cannot map is flagged rather than guessed.

faqs.q: Can it check quantities against drawings?
faqs.a: Not in the first phase. It checks claimed quantities against measurement book entries, BOQ limits and previous bills. Drawing-based quantity take-off is a separate piece of work we can scope later.

faqs.q: Will this create friction with contractors?
faqs.a: The output is an internal verification sheet, and your team decides what to share. Line references often help billing engineers give contractors clearer reasons for each deduction.

faqs.q: How long before it works across all our sites?
faqs.a: After a pilot on one work order, most of the effort is loading BOQs and rules for each new contract. We roll out contractor by contractor, checking each one against past bills before it goes live.
